subject: Behavioral Economics
title: The Baader-Meinhof Phenomenon
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Baader-Meinhof Phenomenon.

hook.text: You learn a new word and suddenly it appears everywhere. It was always there. You just notice now.

buildup.text: After buying a red car, red cars seem to fill every road. The count hasn't changed at all.

discovery.text: This is frequency illusion. Once primed, your brain flags matching info it used to ignore.

twist.text: Confirmation bias then kicks in. Each new sighting reinforces your belief that it's everywhere.

climax.text: The world didn't change. Your filter did. Priming rewires what your brain treats as relevant.

quiz.question: What causes the Baader-Meinhof phenomenon?
options: Your brain starts noticing what it was primed to see
Memory improves after learning something new
